name: Twin Harbours
idea: Two mirrored stone harbours, blue on the left and red on the right. The red well sits on a pillar between their mouths.
hint: Blue first. The red well sits between the harbour mouths; dipping early is fine, the blue well at the bottom left is reusable.

name: Red Door Circuit
idea: A stone shelf splits the field: two gaps on the left, and a red door on the right. The red well sits on the shelf.
hint: As blue, the gaps on the left are the only way up. Once red, break the red door on the right and it becomes a short way between floors.

name: Return Ticket
idea: A red-capped vault beside the blue well keeps blue inside, and a red plug sits on the well. Turn red to open both, then return to blue.
hint: Blue → red → blue. Red opens the vault caps and the plug on the blue well; then dip blue to finish the vault. ↻ restarts instantly.

name: Keep the Return
idea: A disposable roof, two paints and a layered vault. Decide when the quick rebound will be most useful.
hint: Grey gives just one rebound. When will it help most? Breaking it early is recoverable.

name: Open Your Way Back
idea: A sealed blue well and a red vault with blue inside. Prepare a route before committing to a new colour.
hint: Which route will you need after turning red? R restarts if your plan fails.

name: Unlock the Loop
idea: Red paint lies beyond a locked gate. The vault needs both colours, so plan more than the outward trip.
hint: Find the key, then work out how to bring both colours to the vault.

name: Paint Shuttle
idea: A low shuttle lane with paint at both ends. Stone roofs turn you down into the wells quickly.
hint: Blue and red wells are reusable. Use stone to shorten rebounds; grey bumpers give one bounce, then disappear.

name: Broken Staircase
idea: Offset ledges and temporary grey steps. Break a step for a shortcut, or keep it for a quick rebound.
hint: Blue and red wells are reusable. Use stone to shorten rebounds; grey bumpers give one bounce, then disappear.

name: Switchyard
idea: Irregular stone islands split a compact field into bounce pockets, with red and blue targets on different approaches.
hint: Blue and red wells are reusable. Use stone to shorten rebounds; grey bumpers give one bounce, then disappear.

name: Paint Shuttle · fast
idea: Same shuttle layout at 12 cells/s vertically and 7 sideways.
hint: Blue and red wells are reusable. Use stone to shorten rebounds; grey bumpers give one bounce, then disappear.

name: Paint Shuttle · accelerating
idea: Same shuttle layout: start at 9 cells/s, accelerate to 16 in free flight, reset to 9 on impact.
hint: Blue and red wells are reusable. Use stone to shorten rebounds; grey bumpers give one bounce, then disappear.

name: Layer Cake
idea: A blue shell hides red; red hides blue. Each broken layer opens the next approach.
hint: Blue → red → blue. Drop into the blue or red wells at the bottom to repaint; clear both layers before diamonds.

name: Opposite Vaults
idea: Two vaults reverse the colour order. Revisit the blue and red dipping wells to open their centres.
hint: Blue → red → blue opens both vaults. Reuse the bottom wells; each shell hides the other colour.

name: Three-way Return
idea: Blue opens red, red opens green, and green reveals blue again. Three reusable wells serve one layered vault.
hint: Blue → red → green → blue. Dip in the matching bottom well whenever you need to change colour.

name: Twin Islands
idea: Blue island first, then red. Stone caps and floors preserve tight bounce lanes around both islands.
hint: Clear every blue block, including the paint guard at far right. Slide into red paint, clear red, then collect diamonds.

name: Open the Heart
idea: Blue surrounds a red core. A permanent central spine and outer rails keep short rebounds as you carve.
hint: Finish the blue shell before entering red paint at the right edge. Work both sides of the stone spine to clear red.

name: Across the Terraces
idea: Blue terraces lead to a key-operated gate. Beyond it, red shelves form a final chamber.
hint: Fetch the key on the left, clear blue, then open the gate in the lower dividing wall. Red paint waits inside the right chamber.

name: Rattle Rows
idea: 1-row channels between block bands, with stone ribs every 4 rows so a cleared band never becomes a hall.
hint: Clear each band from the channel under it. The red pot is at the right end of a channel: slide into it only when blue is done.

name: Switchback
idea: A snake corridor: stone shelves with one gap at alternate ends. Grey bricks in the shelves are shortcuts.
hint: Wind up through the gaps. The red pot is at the right end of the fourth channel: slide into it when blue is done.

name: Pockets
idea: 2×2 rooms fenced by blocks, with stone posts at the corners. The ball rattles inside and breaks into the next room.
hint: Blue only. Break a fence to get into the next room. Posts never break.

name: Shafts
idea: Short vertical shafts between stone columns. Windows in the columns are grey, plugs in the floors are blue.
hint: Blue only. Bounce up a shaft, then break a grey window or a blue plug to move on.

name: Grey Scaffold
idea: A grey lattice you carve through, held up by stone ribs so the carving never opens a hall.
hint: Grey breaks in any colour. Blue first, then slide sideways into the red pot on the right.

name: Colour Onion
idea: Four colour layers from the bottom up, each sealed by a stone rib. The next colour's pot waits at the end of the layer's channel.
hint: Blue, red, green, gold, from the bottom up. Each pot waits at the end of a channel, behind that layer's last block.

name: Stone Heavy
idea: Close to the density reference: about a third of the field is stone and the corridors are fixed.
hint: Stone never breaks. Follow the corridors and touch every blue block.

name: Brick Wall
idea: Almost all coloured bricks: you carve every corridor yourself. Two stone ribs stop it turning into one big hall.
hint: Blue, then red from the pot at the right edge, then the diamonds.

name: Narrow Eight
idea: The rattle-row idea on an 8-column grid: bigger tiles on the phone, shorter channels.
hint: Clear the blue bands, then the red ones. The red pot is at the right end of the rib: slide into it when blue is done.

name: Open Field
idea: Contrast: sparse blocks and long flights, built for speed routes rather than corridors.
hint: Few blocks, lots of air. Blue first, then the red pot in the corner, then red.
